lessons: Keep the design as is: node-span scalar substitution, real-loader validation of the temp file, no-overwrite publish for backup and temp, and cleanup on failure. The reviewer found the logic sound; only test coverage and one message are missing.

Add refusal cases to test_migrate_refuses_invalid_inputs_without_a_write using raw text: invalid YAML ('schema_version: 0\n  bad: ['), a list document, a scalar document, schema_version: true, and schema_version: 0.0. Assert bytes unchanged, no .bak, no .migrate.tmp.
Add a test_config.py case where a version-1 config has an unknown key or invalid value: migrate must raise ConfigError, leave bytes unchanged, and create no .bak or temp file.
Add at least the invalid-YAML and non-mapping (list document) cases to the CLI refusal parametrization in tests/test_cli.py, asserting EXIT_REFUSED, config unchanged, and no .bak.

On FileExistsError from publishing the temp file, raise a ConfigError that names the stale file and its release, e.g. 'stale .config.yaml.migrate.tmp from an interrupted migration; remove it and rerun'.
Add a test that pre-creates .config.yaml.migrate.tmp and asserts: the refusal message names the file and says to remove it, config bytes are unchanged, and no .bak is created.
reason: Review snagged on fixable test-coverage gaps and one missing paved-road message. The implementation design was judged sound, so a retry at the same capability should succeed.
